root_idea.summary: The root centers on interpenetration, joining, or the bringing of things into contact. In the mental domain, doubt is understood as two incompatible possibilities being brought together without a settled judgment.
root_idea.development: Concrete extensions include piercing, fastening, close connection, grouping, and being equipped with interconnected arms. The meaning of doubt develops from alternatives being confused or joined so that the mind finds no firm point of reliance.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested nominal form and is presented under the normalized dictionary headword شَكّ.

senses.definition: Doubt or uncertainty: a state in which two incompatible possibilities remain unsettled in the mind.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, the doubt may concern whether something exists, what kind of thing it is, one of its qualities, or the purpose for which it exists. It is narrower than sheer lack of knowledge and may occur in constructions such as being in doubt about something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To doubt, waver, or be uncertain about something; said of an affair, to become dubious or confused.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be used with فِي for the matter about which one is uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be difficult, hard, or distressing to someone; in another reported interpretation, to occasion doubt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a case or affair that presents difficulty or uncertainty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To limp or halt slightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a camel, including a slight lameness of the hind leg or an arm held against the side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cleaving or sticking closely to another thing; close union, including close relationship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical use extends to things or relationships that become closely attached.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on or attire oneself completely with arms or weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction شَكَّ فِي السِّلَاحِ describes entering amid or being fully covered by one's weapons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pierce or transpierce someone or something with a spear, arrow, or similar weapon; in one usage, to pierce two things together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may emphasize joining the pierced objects on the weapon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To traverse, cross, or cut through countries or districts in order to reach someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an extended use of the piercing or cutting-through sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw, join, or adjoin one thing to another; said of a garment, to draw it together and fasten it, or to let it hang down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning also occurs in expressions of things being conjoined or grasped together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place tents in one regular row or series, near together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a conventional plural-verb construction describing an orderly arrangement of tents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make relationships closely connected, or to assert that someone is connected with another's lineage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive use can describe a person being made or asserted to belong to another lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make the stitch-holes in a garment far apart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This specialized sewing use is reported with a meaning opposite to close joining.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To incline toward, trust, rely, or rest upon someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is distinguished by the kasra in the first radical and expresses reliance or finding ease in the relied-upon object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to doubt, waver, or become uncertain about something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative Form II construction places the affected person in doubt regarding the matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A day whose position in the calendar is uncertain, especially the day that may be either the end of Shaʿbān or the beginning of Ramaḍān.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for uncertainty between the last day of one month and the first of the next.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small crack in a bone.
A seam or line of sewing in a garment.
A coat of mail composed of narrow rings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported as an attributed lexical gloss and is distinct from the ordinary noun meaning “doubt.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Arsenic or ratsbane, a poisonous medicament used to destroy rats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The substance is described as occurring in white and yellow kinds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covering placed over the two curved extremities of a bow.
A single piercing through two riders on a horse.
A distant region or stretch of country toward which one directs oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is equated with شُقَّةٌ in the cited idiom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Arms or weapons worn on the body.
A broad piece of wood inserted into the handle-hole of an axe or similar tool to narrow and secure it.
Discordance in natural dispositions or character.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression مُخْتَلِفُ الشِّكَّةِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that limps or halts because of slight lameness.
Persons who claim a relationship they do not properly possess, including alleged or adopted sons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is reported as a plural expression for people involved in a disputed claim of lineage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tents arranged in a row.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may be used of pitching tents in one line, though an alternative derivation is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel whose fatness is uncertain because thick fur conceals whether her hump is full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized, figurative description of uncertainty about the animal's condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sides or lateral portions.
A region, quarter, tract, or section of land.
A party, sect, distinct body, or class of people; in the plural, distinct bodies of soldiers.
A way, course, mode, or manner of acting or conducting oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عَلَى شَكِيكَتِهِ, “following his way or manner.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Natural disposition or character.
A basket used for holding fruit.
Joined pieces of wood forming the tent-like tops of covered vehicles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This plural technical use refers to the wooden framework of a هَوْدَج.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vulgar term for a woman regarded as well-proportioned, beautiful, slender, active, and clever.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry explicitly restricts this colloquial application to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficult, said of a bit or bridle.
Sharp arms or weapons, or the sharpness of arms or weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may denote either the weapons themselves or their sharpness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Completely armed or clad in a full set of weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in constructions describing a person or group fully equipped with arms or iron armor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A close or near relationship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional description of closely united kinship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tumour in the throat or fauces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is reported especially in connection with children.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thong used to join or fasten parts of a coat of mail.
Doubted or subject to doubt, said of an affair or case.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited expression is مَشْكُوكٌ فِيهِ or an affair described as containing doubt.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made firm or strong, said of a pulpit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate reported use, equivalent to مَشْدُودٌ.

cautions: The Lane match is based on contraction of the geminated QAC root شكك to the Lane root شك.
The Quranic form in this packet is the noun شَكّ; the many additional senses are Classical Arabic uses of homonymous or derived forms and are kept separate from the Quranic sense.
